clue.text: Essential requirement for operating a slot machine

definitions.text: Essential requirement for operating a slot machine

parts.words: Essential requirement for operating a slot machine
parts.note: a fruit machine only takes coins, so the thing you cannot do without is ready money in metal form

explanation.surface: A dry description of what a gambler needs before playing a fruit machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'hard' literally: coins are hard, unlike notes or cards, and a slot takes only coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is what any machine demands, and coins are literally solid, so the phrase fits both senses.

clue.text: The laughing stock of Africa?

parts.note: stock means animals, and the African scavengers known for their laugh-like call are this laughing population

explanation.surface: Seems to name someone mocked across a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laughing stock' means a figure of fun, but split it: 'stock' is animals, and these ones famously 'laugh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted scavengers of the African savannah make a cackling cry, so they are the continent's laughing beasts.

clue.text: Primate replaced ushers

indicators.note: re-placed: the letters of ushers are put in new places

explanation.surface: A senior bishop has substituted the cathedral ushers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests a churchman, but it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian macaque is a monkey, and monkeys belong to the order of primates.

clue.text: Reckoning that comes to nothing

parts.note: a reckoning of numbers backwards that finishes on zero, as before a launch

explanation.surface: Sounds like a calculation that proves futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes to nothing' suggests failure, but here it means the counting ends at zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting backwards to zero before a rocket launch or the New Year ends literally at nought.

clue.text: Travelling light?

parts.note: a meteor is a light that streaks across the sky, so it is literally a light on the move

explanation.surface: Suggests packing only hand luggage for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling light' is the idiom for carrying little luggage; read literally it is a moving light in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor burning up is seen as a streak of light racing across the night sky.

clue.text: Deal turned out well

definitions.meaning: deal is soft timber from fir or pine, and this conifer supplies such wood
smartly dressed, neat and trim in appearance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like a business agreement or a hand of cards, but here it is a kind of softwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is the timber of firs such as this tree; someone smartly turned out is also described with the same adjective.

clue.text: Born under Victoria, true

indicators.note: in a down clue the born letter sits below the fruit

parts.note: the Victoria is a popular English variety of plum

explanation.surface: Someone born in Queen Victoria's reign, it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen, but it is a variety of plum.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb line hangs exactly vertical, so plumb means true, perfectly upright.

clue.text: Disturbance that may have Paul upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these two words' letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A disturbance that might leave a man called Paul upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent change or disruption is a disturbance, literally a heaving up.

clue.text: Hasten construction of deep exit

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are built into something new

explanation.surface: Urges builders to hurry up with a deep exit tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed up a process is to hasten it.

clue.text: He has the will to settle things

definitions.text: He has the will to settle things

parts.words: He has the will to settle things
parts.note: the person named in a testament to carry it out holds that document and settles the estate

explanation.surface: Seems to praise a determined person who resolves problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as determination, but it is the legal document; 'settle things' means winding up the dead person's affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The person appointed in a testament administers it, distributing the estate as the deceased directed.

clue.text: Gag produces a quiet admonition at university

parts.note: hush is what you say to tell someone to be quiet
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A joke is told to an audience: a word of reproof heard on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag someone is to silence them or suppress news, which is what covering something up by silence means.

clue.text: Take on tea in a bag, paying in instalments

parts.note: to take on staff is to hire them

indicators.note: the tea word goes inside the bag word

parts.note: a purse is a small bag
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Instructions for teabags, apparently, mixed with a payment plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Hire purchase is the British name for buying on credit by instalments, owning the goods only after the last payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Under this British credit arrangement the buyer pays by regular sums, gaining ownership at the end.

clue.text: Responsible person gives notice last month

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Someone sensible put up an announcement a few weeks ago.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is old commercial Latin for 'of last month', as in 'your letter of the 5th ult.'
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is expected to act responsibly, as opposed to a child.

clue.text: Dog food from the back of a lorry?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail them
board means meals, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Pet food fell off the back of a lorry, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog food' looks like one item, but 'Dog' is a verb for following.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the hinged flap at the rear of a truck that drops down for loading.

clue.text: Token expletive in defiant response

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
blast is a mild curse

explanation.surface: Someone swears in a token gesture of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous retort hitting back at an attack or criticism is a forceful defiant reply.

clue.text: Low joints for workers? That's outstanding!

definitions.meaning: worker bees have leg joints, low down on their bodies
an exclamation of high praise for something excellent

explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' are worker bees, and their 'low joints' are knees; the phrase is also slang for the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises something superb, and literally names the knee joints of the insect workers in a hive.

clue.text: Came with rice to provide dessert?

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged to provide something new

explanation.surface: Something arrived with the rice to serve as pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' signals that the letters of CAME and RICE are remade into the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen sweet served after the main course is a typical dessert, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: One who profits from workers' activity?

definitions.text: One who profits from workers' activity?

parts.words: One who profits from workers' activity?
parts.note: worker bees make honey, and the keeper of their hives gains from it

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a capitalist exploiting labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' sounds like employees but means worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper collects the honey and wax that worker bees produce.

clue.text: Common drinking companions

parts.note: two pieces of crockery always seen together when tea is drunk, so they are companions in drinking

explanation.surface: Sounds like ordinary pub mates out for a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking companions' suggests people, but the pair are items of tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: The teacup and its dish routinely go together, the most familiar pairing at any tea table.

clue.text: Go for help

definitions.meaning: to prefer or choose, as in opting for one side
a kindness or good turn done for someone

explanation.definitionFit: To prefer something is one sense; a kind deed done for someone is the other, the same word in both.

clue.text: They're enormous soldier ants

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Claims that soldier ants are huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier ants' reads as a kind of insect, but 'soldier' is GI.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge beings of legend, and any very large people or things, are giants.

clue.text: Sailor can brew tea at first for the coach

indicators.note: tells us the tea word is placed at the very start of the answer

parts.note: char is slang for tea
AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: to brew is to stir up or concoct, so the letters of can are mixed

explanation.surface: A sailor makes tea in a can before boarding the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' gives ANC, the anagram of 'can'; 'at first' puts the tea word at the front. A charabanc is an old open-topped British excursion coach.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned motor coach for day trips and outings went by this name, from French char-à-bancs.

clue.text: A right outsider

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone backing a long shot that is truly a rank outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A right outsider' reads as 'a real outsider'; 'right' is the legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner, someone from elsewhere, is an outsider to a community.

clue.text: Uniform colour of Gurkha kit

indicators.note: the colour is taken out of the run of letters in these two words

explanation.surface: Describes the colour of a Gurkha soldier's uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: This dull brownish-yellow is the standard shade of army dress.

clue.text: Miracle drug for backside beset by nettle

indicators.note: the back half of 'backside' tells us the whole assembly is read backwards
the side is surrounded by the irritating word

parts.note: to nettle is to irritate or rile
XI is a team of eleven, a side in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A wonder cure for a bottom stung by nettles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backside' is split in two: 'side' is the eleven-a-side team in Roman numerals, and 'back' reverses everything, turning RIXILE into the answer. 'beset by' puts the team inside the irritation word.
explanation.definitionFit: A magical cure-all potion, sought by alchemists, is the classic wonder remedy.

clue.text: Oarsman returned in vessel, showing distress

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the container

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel

indicators.note: the oarsman word comes back the other way

parts.note: an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A rower comes back to his boat looking upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives REWOR, which goes 'in' CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A face lined and haggard from worry and anxiety shows the strain of long trouble.

clue.text: My unit represented in strike

indicators.note: re-presented, these letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A soldier says his unit took part in a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' is read as re-presented, laid out again in a different order.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a refusal to work, and a revolt against commanders is the military equivalent.

clue.text: Steps taken in yards or metres

definitions.meaning: actions taken to deal with something, as in government action
units of length are units of quantity

explanation.surface: Footsteps counted out in imperial or metric units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like paces measured in yards, but it means actions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: official actions, and standard units such as the yard and metre.
